what_happened: The job moved the readers of records/ to the athena/records worktree, with per-reader tests. It was rejected at the final verdict. 3 of 10 acceptance criteria were unmet, with 2 major findings. No failed checks are listed. The first unmet criterion needs a named worktree test for each reachable reader. Each test plants different records in the worktree and in-tree and asserts the worktree's are returned. The findings say two groups of tests do not do this. The scoring tests never run the scoring code, so reverting run.rs or manage.rs would leave them passing. The introspect, backtest and proposals tests call helper functions, not the readers. The second unmet criterion needs scoring's use of the worktree regardless of the head passed to be documented in docs/decisions.md and tested. The third needs the change description to list every reader, map each to its tests, and cite commands actually run. Those two are unmet, but the findings do not detail why. The other 7 criteria were met, so the code change itself may be sound.
cause: Nothing in code checks, before handover, that each reader-test calls the real reader and fails if the reader is reverted. The criteria name many readers, and the producer wrote tests that exercise helpers beside the readers. This is the retry of the same reader move (20261026-155302-zdnq), and it fixed the missing tests but not their depth. Nothing lists the readers from the code and ties each test to the entry point that reader runs through. Only the verifier's judgment at the final verdict catches shallow tests, and there rejection is the only outcome. The reading also does not say that a test must fail when the reader is reverted. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show what the producer ran or wrote.
prevention: Add a pre-handover check for reader-move jobs. It would enumerate the readers by grep and require, for each, a named test that calls the reader's real entry point. It would also run a mutation step: revert each reader to the in-tree path and confirm its test fails. The producer would have to pass this check before it hands over, and the check's output would go into the change description. A criterion that names a reader would be accepted only when it names the entry point the test must call.
proposed_request: Retry job 20261026-170042-cgq9: finish moving all readers of records/ to the athena/records worktree, with in-tree records/ as the fallback. Fix the tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/records_branch_readers.rs. Each athena-cli-reachable reader (Records::load_current, RecordSet::load_current, read_records, introspect walks, scoring, forecasting, retry carry, auditor, proposals, backtest) needs a named worktree test and a named fallback test. Each worktree test must create the records worktree under a temporary state directory and plant different records in the worktree and in-tree. It must call the reader's real entry point, not a helper, and assert the worktree's records are returned. For scoring, run the real scoring code path (run.rs and manage.rs), so that reverting it makes the test fail. For introspect, backtest and proposals, call the actual reader, not the helper functions. Document in docs/decisions.md that scoring uses the worktree regardless of the head passed, and test it. Before handover, revert each reader to the in-tree path one at a time and confirm its worktree test fails, then restore it. The change description must list every reader found by grep and map each to its worktree and fallback test names and the observed marker. It must state the walltime (xtask) and land_pr (gh.rs) placements, say that common-dir derivation is new code and not a repair, and cite commands actually run, including cargo test --locked. Keep the production changes from the earlier attempt.
